hyperedges.relationship: Backup flow: engine hashes files, exchanges manifest for dedup, then streams only needed files via gRPC
Watcher pipeline: fsnotify event -> debounce 500ms -> stability gate 60s -> ongoing backup upload
Security+storage model: passphrase derived to master key via Argon2id, per-file DEK for AES-GCM, content addressed by BLAKE3 hash
All gRPC services require mutual TLS with Ed25519 certificates signed by shared CA
Scheduler triggers remote backups by sending TriggerBackup RPC to online clients tracked in registry
Web UI uses HTMX for server-driven updates, Alpine.js for client state, SSE for real-time notifications
NAT clients maintain persistent tunnel stream to server; server dispatches commands via tunnel hub; registry tracks tunnel connections
Retention engine evaluates policies against DB entries, marks expired versions, deletes orphaned storage files
Cross-client restore: server decrypts source backup, streams to target client over gRPC, requires target online
After backup completes, client updates local DB then streams entire database to server via SyncDatabase RPC
A full backup processes all files within include paths that are not matched by exclude patterns
Auto backup is triggered by the file watcher detecting changes in configured include paths
Remote client restore decrypts backup data using passphrase and transfers via gRPC to client or server filesystem
Client registry tracks connections received via gRPC and surfaces status on clients page
Retention engine periodically evaluates policies against backup records to purge expired versions
Dashboard aggregates all system health metrics into a unified overview
Node role determines capabilities: server mode enables gRPC client serving, hybrid adds local watcher and backups
Deduplication operates across full and ongoing backups to reduce storage by eliminating redundant file content
